messages:
mira: Heads up — had a call with Azure procurement. They pushed back on a straight EDP for GPUs. Proposed a "spot-to-dedicated swap" clause that lets them convert a portion of committed GPUs to spot with invoice credits if capacity isn't available. Thoughts?

alex: Can you paste the suggested language they sent?

mira: ```
Clause 7.4 (Spot-to-Dedicated Swap): Provider may convert up to 35% of the committed GPU capacity to Preemptible/Spot instances during supply constraints. If Provider cannot provide equivalent dedicated capacity within 72 hours, Provider shall issue invoice credits equal to 1.5x the average per-GPU hourly rate for the affected hours, capped at the monthly committed spend. Provider to notify Customer >=48 hours before large-scale conversion (>10% of committed capacity).
```

ton y: We should avoid taking a straight 35% convertible floor. Too much tail risk. :thinking_face:

contracts-bot: Uploaded draft contract: /drive/contracts/azure-risk-share-draft-v1.docx :paperclip:

legal: Skimmed — two flags: (1) Their audit rights are broader than acceptable, (2) The proposed credit cap being 'monthly committed spend' wipes out recourse on long outages. Need to narrow scope and add true-up window.

alex: What if we counter with a hybrid: 25% convertible, 75% guaranteed, plus a 'credits-on-failure' ladder: 72-168h outage -> 1.5x rate, >168h -> 2x rate, subject to quarterly reconciliation? Also require 48h notice for conversions and limit to 2 conversions per rolling 90 days.

procurement: They came back asking for 30% regional carveouts (they want rights to convert per-region) rather than global %. Can we accept a 2-region guarantee instead of global?

mira: Numbers check — target 18mo commitment ~ $12.3M list. If we accept 30% regional carveouts our utilization uncertainty rises ~12% based on prior quarter usage patterns. Quick calc:
```
Committed list: $12,300,000
Estimated utilization hit if 30% carveout: +12% cost = ~$1.48M
Rebate potential with credits ladder ~ 0.6% - 1.8% of spend depending on outage windows
```

tony: Operationally we can mitigate by asking for monthly capacity reconciliation + quarterly true-up (delay true-up settlement by 30 days) — that reduces billing shock and gives us time to shift workloads.

legal: Add explicit SLA credit formula into the contract (tie credits to measured availability per-region and make audit rights scoped and timeboxed to quarterly reconciliations). Remove perpetual unrestricted audit clause.

contracts-bot: I'll generate a redline with the risk-sharing ladder and regional carveout limits and post to vendors channel by EOD.

mira: :thumbsup: I'll update the commitment model with these parameters and run sensitivity. @alex @tony please review before noon tomorrow.
